questions.question: What is the operating principle of a 3-Phase Induction Motor?

options.A: Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction and production of Rotating Magnetic Field

questions.question: The synchronous speed (Ns) of a 3-phase AC machine having 'P' poles supplied with frequency 'f' Hz is given by:
What is the synchronous speed of a 4-pole, 3-phase induction motor operating on a 50 Hz AC supply?

options.A: 3000 rpm

questions.question: The rotor speed (N) of a 3-phase induction motor is always:

options.A: Greater than synchronous speed (Ns)

questions.question: Slip (s) of a 3-phase induction motor is defined by the formula:

options.A: s = (Ns - N) / Ns

questions.question: At standstill (when rotor speed N = 0), the slip (s) of an induction motor is:
What is the rotor frequency (fr) of an induction motor running at slip 's' with supply frequency 'f'?

options.A: fr = f / s

questions.question: If a 6-pole, 50 Hz 3-phase induction motor operates at 4% slip, what is the frequency of induced rotor currents?

options.A: 50 Hz

questions.question: In a 3-phase squirrel cage induction motor, rotor slots are slightly skewed (tilted) in order to:

options.A: Reduce magnetic locking (cogging) between stator and rotor and eliminate humming noise

questions.question: What is 'Cogging' in a 3-phase induction motor?

options.A: Overheating of stator windings
options.B: Magnetic locking of rotor teeth with stator teeth when number of stator slots equals rotor slots

questions.question: What is 'Crawling' in a 3-phase induction motor?

options.A: Motor running at near zero speed due to open circuit
options.B: Motor running steadily at a fraction (e.g., 1/7th) of synchronous speed due to space harmonics

questions.question: Which type of 3-phase induction motor permits external resistance to be added to the rotor circuit for speed control and high starting torque?

options.A: Squirrel Cage Induction Motor

questions.question: What is the condition for maximum starting torque (Tst) in a 3-phase induction motor?

options.A: Rotor resistance R2 equals rotor standstill reactance X2 (R2 = X2)

questions.question: What is the condition for maximum running torque (Tmax) of a 3-phase induction motor?

options.A: R2 = X2

questions.question: Double squirrel cage rotors are designed to provide:

options.A: High starting torque with low starting current
options.C: Low starting torque with high speed

questions.question: In a double squirrel cage rotor, the outer cage is made of high resistance material (brass/bronze) and has:

options.A: High resistance and low reactance

questions.question: Why is Direct-On-Line (DOL) starting limited to small 3-phase induction motors (usually up to 5 HP)?

options.A: Because starting torque is zero
options.B: Because starting current is very high (5 to 7 times full load current) causing line voltage dips

questions.question: When a 3-phase induction motor is started using a Star-Delta starter, the starting line current is reduced to what fraction of DOL starting current?
When started using a Star-Delta starter, the starting torque of the induction motor becomes:

options.A: 1 / 3 of direct-on-line starting torque

questions.question: Auto-transformer starters are used for starting large 3-phase induction motors because they allow:

options.A: Tapping selection to adjust starting voltage and current

questions.question: What test on a 3-phase induction motor is equivalent to the Short-Circuit test of a transformer?

options.A: No-Load Test

questions.question: No-Load Test on a 3-phase induction motor is conducted to determine:

options.A: Full-load copper loss
options.B: Constant losses (Stator core loss + Friction and windage loss) and magnetizing current

questions.question: A Circle Diagram of a 3-phase induction motor can be drawn using data from:

options.A: No-load test, Blocked rotor test, and Stator resistance test

questions.question: The Circle Diagram of an induction motor can be used to predict:

options.A: Efficiency, power factor, slip, maximum torque, and output power at any load

questions.question: What is 'Single Phasing' in a 3-phase induction motor?

options.A: Running the motor on 1-phase AC by choice
options.B: Accidental opening of one phase line of a running 3-phase motor due to blown fuse or loose contact

questions.question: If a running 3-phase induction motor experiences Single Phasing under full load, what will happen?

options.A: It will stop immediately without taking current
options.B: It will continue to run, but draw dangerously heavy current in remaining 2 phases and eventually burn if not tripped
options.D: It will operate normally without any temperature rise

questions.question: Speed control of a 3-phase induction motor by Pole Changing method provides:

options.A: Continuous stepless speed control
options.C: Speed control above synchronous speed only

questions.question: In Variable Voltage Variable Frequency (VVVF) drives used in modern Metro Railway 3-phase AC traction (3-phase VVVF traction):

options.A: V/f ratio is kept constant to maintain constant magnetic flux density and constant torque capability
options.B: Voltage is kept constant while frequency is varied
options.C: Frequency is kept constant while voltage is doubled
options.D: Motor operates only at synchronous speed

questions.question: Synchronous speed of an AC motor can be varied by changing:

options.A: Rotor resistance
options.B: Supply frequency (f) or Number of stator poles (P)

questions.question: Why are single-phase induction motors NOT self-starting?

options.A: Single phase supply produces a pulsating magnetic field instead of a rotating magnetic field

questions.question: According to Double Field Revolving Theory, a pulsating 1-phase magnetic field is equivalent to two rotating fields of equal magnitude rotating in:

options.A: Same direction at same speed
options.B: Opposite directions at same synchronous speed

questions.question: Which component is connected in series with the auxiliary (starting) winding of a Capacitor Start Single Phase Induction Motor to disconnect it after accelerating?

options.A: Centrifugal Switch

questions.question: The centrifugal switch in a capacitor-start motor opens when the motor reaches approximately what percentage of synchronous speed?
Which single-phase induction motor provides highest starting torque?

options.A: Split-phase motor

questions.question: Which single-phase motor is most widely used in ceiling fans and small ventilation fans in Metro stations?

options.A: Permanent Split Capacitor (Capacitor-run) Motor

questions.question: Which single-phase motor has low efficiency, low starting torque, and uses a copper shading ring around a portion of each salient pole?

options.A: Capacitor Start Motor

questions.question: A Universal Motor can run on:

options.A: AC supply only

questions.question: A Universal Motor is essentially a modified:

options.A: DC Series Motor

questions.question: Which small motor is used in portable hand drills, domestic food mixers, and vacuum cleaners due to high speed at light loads?

options.A: Universal Motor

questions.question: What is a Synchronous Motor?

options.A: An AC motor that runs at constant speed (Synchronous Speed Ns) from no load to full load
options.B: A motor whose speed drops linearly with load
options.D: An induction motor with open rotor

questions.question: Why is a 3-phase Synchronous Motor NOT self-starting?

options.A: Due to high inertia of the rotor, unidirectional torque is not developed as stator magnetic poles rotate rapidly past stationary rotor poles
options.B: Because it has no stator field
options.D: Because it operates on DC supply only

questions.question: Damper Windings (Amortisseur windings) fitted in the pole shoes of a synchronous motor serve to:

options.A: Make the motor self-starting as an induction motor and suppress Hunting oscillations during sudden load changes

questions.question: What is 'Hunting' in a Synchronous Motor?

options.A: Oscillation of the rotor around its equilibrium position during sudden load fluctuations

questions.question: An Over-excited Synchronous Motor running on no-load draws current at what power factor?

options.A: Lagging Power Factor

questions.question: An over-excited synchronous motor operated on no-load to improve power factor of industrial power networks is called a:

options.A: Synchronous Condenser (or Synchronous Capacitor)

questions.question: Under-excited synchronous motors operate at what power factor?

options.A: Leading

questions.question: What shape do the curves representing Armature Current vs Field Current of a Synchronous Motor at constant load resemble?

options.A: 'V' Curves

questions.question: In a Synchronous Machine, the Inverted V-Curves represent the variation of:

options.A: Power Factor vs Field Current

questions.question: What is an Alternator?

options.A: A Synchronous Generator that converts mechanical power to AC electrical power
options.C: A converter from AC to DC

questions.question: Why do modern commercial Alternators (Synchronous Generators) use a Rotating Field and Stationary Armature structure?

options.A: Easier to insulate high-voltage stationary armature windings; requires only two low-voltage slip rings for DC field excitation

questions.question: Salient pole (projecting pole) type rotors in alternators are used for:

options.A: Low and medium speed prime movers (e.g., Hydro turbines, Diesel engines)

questions.question: Cylindrical (Smooth rotor) type rotors in alternators are designed for:

options.A: High speed operation (1500 rpm or 3000 rpm - Turbo-alternators)

questions.question: What is Pitch Factor (or Coil Span Factor, Kp) of an alternator armature winding?

options.A: Ratio of EMF induced in a short-pitched coil to EMF induced in a full-pitched coil
options.C: Ratio of rotor speed to synchronous speed
options.D: Ratio of active turns to dummy turns

questions.question: Pitch factor (Kp) is calculated using the formula:

options.A: Kp = cos (α / 2) (where α is chording angle)

questions.question: What is Distribution Factor (or Breadth Factor, Kd) of an alternator armature winding?

options.A: Ratio of vector sum of induced EMFs in all coils of a phase group to their arithmetic sum
options.B: Ratio of total slots to total poles
options.C: Ratio of total flux to leakage flux
options.D: Ratio of phase voltage to line voltage

questions.question: Why are short-pitched and distributed windings used in modern alternators?

options.A: To eliminate/reduce unwanted harmonics from output voltage waveform and make it purely sinusoidal
options.C: To increase conductor length and copper loss

questions.question: The induced EMF per phase equation of an Alternator is given by:

options.A: Eph = 4.44 × Kp × Kd × f × Φ × Tph

questions.question: The process of connecting an incoming alternator in parallel with an existing running alternator or infinite busbar is called:

options.A: Synchronization

questions.question: What essential conditions must be satisfied before synchronizing an incoming alternator to an infinite busbar?

options.A: Same terminal voltage, same frequency, same phase sequence, and identical phase angle
options.B: Same kVA rating and same weight
options.C: Same armature resistance and same cooling method

questions.question: Which instrument or device is used to check exact frequency and phase alignment when synchronizing alternators?

options.A: Synchroscope (or 3-Lamp Method)

questions.question: Voltage Regulation of an Alternator is defined as:

options.A: (E0 - V) / V × 100 (where E0 is no-load open circuit voltage and V is full-load terminal voltage)

questions.question: At leading power factor loads, the voltage regulation of an alternator can be:

options.A: Negative

questions.question: Which method of determining alternator voltage regulation is known as the most pessimistic method (gives higher regulation than actual)?

options.A: EMF Method (Synchronous Impedance Method)

questions.question: Which method of determining alternator voltage regulation is known as the optimistic method (gives lower regulation than actual)?

options.A: MMF Method (Ampere-Turn Method)

questions.question: Which method yields the most accurate voltage regulation results for an alternator?

options.A: Potier Triangle (Zero Power Factor - ZPF) Method

questions.question: Synchronous Impedance (Zs) of an alternator is defined as:

options.A: Open Circuit Voltage (E0) / Short Circuit Current (Isc) at same field excitation
options.B: Short Circuit Current / Open Circuit Voltage
options.C: Armature resistance Ra + Inductive reactance Xl

questions.question: The Short Circuit Ratio (SCR) of a Synchronous Machine is defined as:

options.A: Field current required to produce rated voltage on open circuit / Field current required to produce rated current on short circuit
options.B: Short circuit current / Full load current

questions.question: A synchronous machine with a HIGH Short Circuit Ratio (SCR) has:

options.A: Higher stability limit and better voltage regulation but higher short-circuit current

questions.question: Which special single-phase motor operates on the principle of variable reluctance and maintains precise step angular rotation upon receiving digital input pulses?

options.A: Stepper Motor

questions.question: Which non-excited single-phase AC motor has a smooth un-slotted rotor made of hard magnetic cobalt-steel alloy and operates silently?

options.A: Hysteresis Motor

questions.question: Hysteresis Motors are commonly used in sound recording equipment, electric clocks, and tape recorders because of their:

options.A: Extremely quiet, vibrationless operation and constant synchronous speed capability

questions.question: A Reluctance Motor is essentially a single-phase motor with a rotor modified to have:

options.A: Un-equal magnetic reluctance path (salient projections) without rotor windings

questions.question: What happens if two phases of supply to a 3-phase induction motor are interchanged?

options.A: The direction of rotation of the motor will reverse
options.B: The motor will run at double speed
options.C: The motor will burn out immediately
options.D: The motor will run in same direction

questions.question: In a 3-phase slip ring induction motor, adding resistance to the rotor circuit during starting results in:

options.A: Increased starting torque and reduced starting current
options.B: Decreased starting torque and increased starting current

questions.question: In a 3-phase induction motor, full-load slip typically ranges between:
What is the slip of an induction motor when running at synchronous speed (N = Ns)?
If slip 's' becomes negative (s < 0), the induction machine operates in:

options.A: Generating mode (Induction Generator)

questions.question: If slip 's' is greater than 1 (s > 1), the induction machine operates in:

options.A: Plugging (Braking) mode

questions.question: Induction generators are commonly used in:

options.A: Wind power plants and regenerative braking systems connected to grid

questions.question: What is the air gap distance in a 3-phase induction motor compared to a synchronous motor of similar rating?

options.A: Much smaller (to minimize magnetizing current and improve power factor)

questions.question: Magnetizing current drawn by a 3-phase induction motor operates at what power factor?

options.A: Very low lagging power factor (near zero lagging)

questions.question: In a 3-phase induction motor, rotor copper loss is equal to:

options.A: s × Rotor Input Power (s × Pg)

questions.question: Mechanical Power Developed (Pmech) in the rotor of a 3-phase induction motor is equal to:

options.A: (1 - s) × Rotor Input Power (Pg)

questions.question: Ratio of Rotor Copper Loss to Gross Mechanical Power Developed in an induction motor is:
Stator core loss in an induction motor is constant, whereas rotor core loss under normal running condition is:

options.A: Negligible because rotor frequency fr = s × f is very low (1 to 2 Hz)

questions.question: The speed of a 3-phase slip ring induction motor can be controlled from rotor side by:

options.A: Rotor resistance control or Injecting EMF into rotor circuit
options.C: Connecting capacitors in series with stator

questions.question: Kramer and Scherbius drives are speed control systems used for large slip-ring induction motors by:

options.A: Recovering slip power from rotor circuit and feeding it back to supply or shaft

questions.question: Which single-phase motor uses a commutator and short-circuited brushes positioned at an angle to the stator axis?

options.A: Repulsion Motor

questions.question: In modern 3-phase AC traction Metro rakes (e.g., Kolkata Metro AC Rakes), the traction motors used are:

options.A: 3-Phase Squirrel Cage Induction Motors driven by IGBT Inverters
options.B: DC Series Motors with Resistance Grids

questions.question: What is the advantage of 3-Phase AC Traction Motors over DC Traction Motors in Metro trains?

options.A: Higher power-to-weight ratio, robust maintenance-free construction (no commutator/brushes), and easy regenerative braking
options.D: Runs only at single fixed speed

questions.question: The frame of a 3-phase AC induction motor is usually made of:

options.A: Cast iron or fabricated steel

questions.question: What class of insulation is typically used in modern traction induction motors to withstand high thermal stress?

options.A: Class H or Class C (200°C / 180°C rating)

questions.question: In a 3-phase AC machine, the phase difference between magnetic fields produced by each of the three phase windings space-displaced by 120° electrical is:

options.A: 120° electrical

questions.question: Magnitude of the resultant rotating magnetic field produced by a balanced 3-phase stator winding is:

options.A: 1.5 times maximum flux of any individual phase (1.5 Φm)

questions.question: An alternator running in parallel with an infinite busbar has its field excitation increased. What will happen?

options.A: Its reactive power output increases (delivers more lagging VARs), power factor becomes more lagging, but active power output remains unchanged

questions.question: To increase real power (kW) output of an alternator connected to an infinite busbar, one must:

options.A: Increase prime mover mechanical input (governor control)

questions.question: Which protection relay is used to detect internal inter-turn and phase-to-earth faults in large alternators/transformers?

options.A: Merz-Price Differential Protection Relay

questions.question: A Reverse Power Relay is used on an alternator running in parallel to prevent:

options.A: The alternator from acting as a motor and driving the prime mover if prime mover fails

questions.question: What is the standard frequency variation limit allowed in Indian Railway / Metro grid networks as per IE rules?
What type of single-phase motor is used in small timing devices, clocks, and chart recorders?

options.A: Hysteresis or Reluctance Synchronous Motor
